title: "Fundamentals of Computing Systems and Digital Platforms"
toc: false
format: lesson-html
---

This course explains the systems on which games run: the components of
computers and smartphones, operating systems, the mobile platforms Android and
iOS, app stores, networking and cloud computing, and the gaming platforms of
the industry (PC, console, mobile and cloud gaming). It connects each concept
to its effect on game performance, compatibility, testing and publishing.

**Textbook.** Tanenbaum, A. S. and Austin, T. *Structured Computer
Organization*, 6th ed., Pearson, 2012. Reference: Silberschatz, Galvin and
Gagne, *Operating System Concepts*, 10th ed., Wiley, 2018.

**How to study each lesson.** Read the lesson notes (PDF) before and after the
lecture. Use the interactive lesson page to practise: it has questions with
instant feedback, simulators and mini-games (the PDF links to them with QR
codes). The slides are a short summary for revision.

## Units

The course in teaching order: 12 units and 2 practice weeks. Each unit has
a lecture and a seminar of 60 minutes, and a homework: the seminar
practises the lecture of the same unit. A practice week (dashed, tagged
*Flexible*) has no new ideas: case studies and the project presentations.
It is taught when time allows; otherwise study it at home, because every
answer is on the page. Faded sessions are not available yet.
